verdict.rationale: Letta ships an explicit shared-memory feature: a Git-backed shared memory repository that multiple agents can read/write via `letta shared-memory create --name team-memory`, giving agents a common working context (letta-docs-8, letta-docs-21, letta-docs-29). This is opt-in and separate from an agent's own private memory blocks, implying private memory stays private by default, but the docs never explicitly describe access-control/permission boundaries between users or tenants sharing the same memory. Missing for 10: explicit per-user/tenant permission controls on shared memory, documentation of how privacy is enforced when multiple users touch the same shared repo, and independent/hands-on verification of isolation.
